Myopia, or short-sightedness, is rising rapidly among children across India. While a mild prescription may seem manageable, unchecked progression in childhood can lead to significantly higher prescriptions and a greater risk of serious eye conditions in adulthood.
Children with myopia see nearby objects clearly but struggle with distant ones. They may squint frequently, sit closer to screens, or seem inattentive during outdoor activities. Many parents discover the issue only during a school checkup. A family history of myopia, excessive near work, reduced outdoor time, and prolonged screen use are all known risk factors.
High myopia — prescriptions beyond minus 6 diopters — is associated with increased risk of retinal detachment, glaucoma, and macular degeneration later in life, making early intervention essential.
Today, myopia management extends beyond glasses. Specially designed contact lenses, low-dose atropine eye drops, and at least one hour of outdoor activity daily have all been shown to slow progression meaningfully.

Fatigue, breathlessness, pale skin, and persistent weakness are symptoms many women dismiss as a result of a busy life. In many cases, however, these are signs of iron deficiency anaemia — one of the most common yet underdiagnosed conditions in women.
Iron is essential for producing haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen through the body. When iron levels are too low, tissues and organs receive less oxygen, leaving the body exhausted. Women are particularly vulnerable due to monthly menstrual blood loss, and risk increases further during pregnancy and after delivery.
Heavy periods, a diet low in iron-rich foods, poor absorption, and frequent pregnancies are common contributing factors. Left untreated, anaemia can impair concentration, reduce immunity, affect foetal growth, and increase the risk of preterm delivery.
A simple blood test can diagnose anaemia and identify its cause. Treatment includes dietary changes, iron supplements, and in some cases intravenous iron therapy — alongside addressing the root cause, whether it is menstrual irregularities, fibroids, or nutritional gaps.
At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Dr. Shilpa Jaypuriya provides personalised and compassionate care, helping women in Virar identify and manage anaemia effectively.
If you have been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, do not overlook it. Visit Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Virar West, for a complete evaluation.

Many people notice small spots or cobweb-like shapes drifting across their vision, especially against a bright background. These are called floaters, and in most cases they are a natural result of ageing. Knowing when they require urgent attention, however, is important.
Floaters form when tiny clumps develop in the vitreous — the gel inside the eye — and cast shadows on the retina. Flashes of light occur when the vitreous pulls on the retina. While occasional floaters are usually harmless, a sudden increase in their number, new flashes, or a curtain-like shadow across the vision can signal retinal detachment — a serious condition requiring immediate evaluation.
Those with high myopia, a history of eye injury, or prior eye surgery carry greater risk. A dilated retinal examination by an eye specialist can determine whether the floaters are benign or linked to an underlying retinal problem. Retinal tears, if caught early, can be treated effectively with laser before they progress to detachment.
At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre in Virar West, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasises early detection and personalised eye care for retinal and vitreous conditions.

Most of us spend hours every day staring at screens — for work, study, and entertainment. What many people do not realise is that this prolonged screen use quietly strains the eyes in ways that accumulate over time.
Computer Vision Syndrome, also called digital eye strain, causes tired or burning eyes, blurred vision, headaches, and neck discomfort. The eyes must work harder than usual to focus on a screen, particularly in poor lighting or with glare. People with uncorrected refractive errors like myopia or astigmatism are at greater risk, and children attending online classes are increasingly affected.
Simple habits help considerably. Following the 20-20-20 rule — looking at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes — relaxes the eye muscles. Proper screen positioning, adequate room lighting, and a routine eye examination to check for any underlying prescription needs are equally important.

Many people are aware of cataracts and glaucoma, but fewer know about Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), a condition that affects the macula—the central part of the retina responsible for sharp vision. AMD is one of the leading causes of vision impairment in adults above 50 and can affect activities such as reading, driving, recognizing faces, and using mobile phones.

At Jaypuriya Eye and Women Care Centre, Dr. Anand Jaypuriya emphasizes the importance of regular retinal examinations for early detection of age-related eye diseases.

Common symptoms include blurred central vision, difficulty reading, distortion of straight lines, or needing brighter light for routine tasks. While peripheral vision often remains unaffected, central vision can gradually decline if the condition progresses.

Risk factors include increasing age, smoking, high blood pressure, family history, and prolonged exposure to unhealthy lifestyle habits. Regular eye examinations can help identify early changes and allow timely intervention.

Gas & Eye Irritation: Causes & Remedies | ASG Eye Hospital

Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort. 

Common symptoms include:

• Redness
• Burning sensation
• Itching
• Watering eyes
• Dryness
• Blurred vision

These irritants can disrupt the eye's natural tear film, leading to discomfort and increased sensitivity. People with dry eyes, allergies, or contact lenses may be more vulnerable.

To protect your eyes:

• Use lubricating eye drops if recommended
• Improve indoor ventilation
• Avoid smoke and chemical exposure
• Wear protective eyewear in high-risk environments
• Avoid rubbing irritated eyes

If symptoms persist, worsen, or affect your vision, seek professional eye care promptly.
At ASG Eye Hospital, experienced eye specialists provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment for eye irritation, dry eyes, and pollution-related eye problems.

Book an eye consultation with ASG Eye Hospital today to keep your eyes healthy and comfortable.

LASIK vs Contact Lenses – Which is Better for Students? | ASG Eye Hospital

Students today spend long hours studying, attending classes, using digital devices, and participating in sports or extracurricular activities. Clear vision is essential, making many students choose between contact lenses and LASIK surgery.

Contact lenses offer temporary vision correction, but they require daily cleaning, proper hygiene, and ongoing maintenance. Extended wear can sometimes lead to dryness, irritation, and an increased risk of eye infections.

LASIK surgery, on the other hand, provides long-term vision correction and reduces dependence on glasses or contact lenses. For eligible students with a stable eye prescription, 

LASIK offers several advantages:

• Freedom from daily lens maintenance
• No recurring costs for lenses and solutions
• Greater convenience during sports and activities
• Improved comfort during long study sessions
• Reduced dependence on vision correction accessories

Modern LASIK eye surgery uses advanced diagnostic technology to create personalized treatment plans with high precision and safety. Most students can return to their routine within a few days.

At ASG Eye Hospital, experienced eye specialists perform comprehensive evaluations to determine whether LASIK is the right option based on eye health, corneal thickness, and prescription stability.

Book a LASIK consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use
• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced diagnostic technology and experienced specialists help identify early signs of retinal damage and provide timely retina treatment when needed.
Don't wait for symptoms to appear. Regular diabetic eye care and routine retinal examinations can help preserve your vision and support better eye health.

 Allergic Conjunctivitis
Dr. Mohini Modak, Focus Eye Clinic, Thane
Allergic conjunctivitis is a common eye condition caused by allergens such as pollen, dust mites, pet dander, or mold. The most common symptom is intense itching, often affecting both eyes. Patients may also experience redness, watery eyes, and a burning or stinging sensation. Mild swelling of the eyelids and conjunctiva is common, making the eyes look puffy. Many people notice increased sensitivity to light and a feeling of grittiness or irritation, although severe pain is uncommon. Unlike bacterial eye infections, allergic conjunctivitis usually causes a clear, watery discharge rather than thick pus. Symptoms often worsen during allergy seasons or after exposure to allergens and may occur alongside sneezing, a runny nose, or other allergy symptoms. Avoid rubbing your eyes, as this can make symptoms worse. If redness, itching, or watering persists, consult Dr. Mohini Modak at Focus Eye Clinic, Thane, for an accurate diagnosis and personalized treatment to keep your eyes comfortable and healthy.

Eye Checkup Clinic in Thane – The Value of Routine Eye Care

Most people schedule an eye examination only when vision becomes noticeably blurry. Yet many eye conditions develop silently and may not cause symptoms during their early stages.

An Eye Checkup Clinic in Thane serves a much broader purpose than updating spectacle prescriptions. Comprehensive eye examinations can help identify cataracts, glaucoma, retinal conditions, refractive errors, and other vision-related concerns before they begin affecting daily life.

At Focus Eye Clinic, regular screenings are encouraged for children, working professionals, senior citizens, and individuals with health conditions such as diabetes or hypertension. Each stage of life presents different visual demands and eye health considerations.

Think about how often we rely on our vision—whether commuting through busy Thane roads, working on digital screens, studying, or simply spending time with family. Good eyesight influences nearly every aspect of daily living.

Routine eye examinations provide valuable information about both visual performance and overall eye health. In many cases, early detection can lead to simpler management and better long-term outcomes.

Protecting eyesight does not always require waiting for symptoms to appear. Scheduling periodic eye checkups remains one of the most practical steps toward maintaining healthy vision for years ahead.

Side effects of long term steroid use in the eyes

Side Effects of Chronic Steroid Use in the Eyes
Dr. Mohini Modak, Focus Eye Clinic, Thane
Steroid eye drops are highly effective for treating inflammation and allergies, but prolonged or unsupervised use can lead to serious eye problems. One of the most common side effects is an increase in eye pressure, which may result in glaucoma and permanent damage to the optic nerve if left untreated. Long-term steroid use can also accelerate cataract formation, causing blurred vision and reduced clarity. In addition, steroids can slow wound healing, increase the risk of eye infections, and sometimes worsen existing viral or fungal infections by suppressing the eye's natural immune response. Regular eye examinations are essential for anyone using steroid eye drops for an extended period. Never use steroid medications without the guidance of an eye specialist. At Focus Eye Clinic, Thane, Dr. Mohini Modak provides comprehensive eye evaluations, monitors steroid-related side effects, and recommends the safest treatment options to protect your vision. Early detection and proper follow-up can help prevent long-term complications and keep your eyes healthy.

What causes exotropia in adults ?

What Causes Exotropia in Adults?
Exotropia is a condition where one eye turns outward, affecting eye alignment and binocular vision. In adults, exotropia can develop due to several reasons. A common cause is the progression of childhood strabismus that was untreated or inadequately corrected. Neurological conditions such as stroke, brain injury, multiple sclerosis, or nerve palsies can also affect the muscles controlling eye movements, leading to exotropia. Trauma to the eye or orbit, thyroid eye disease, and certain muscle disorders may contribute as well.
Some adults experience exotropia due to age-related weakening of eye muscle control or prolonged visual stress. Symptoms may include double vision, eye strain, headaches, difficulty focusing, and cosmetic concerns.
Early diagnosis is important to identify the underlying cause and prevent worsening symptoms. Treatment options may include prescription glasses, prism lenses, eye exercises, or strabismus surgery depending on the severity and cause.
For expert evaluation and treatment of exotropia, consult Dr. Mohini Modak at Focus Eye Clinic, Thane, where personalized eye care helps restore comfortable and healthy vision.

Children may not complain about blurry vision because they often assume everyone sees the same way they do. This is why many eye problems remain unnoticed during important learning years.

If your child sits too close to the TV, struggles to read the board at school, rubs their eyes frequently, squints often, or complains of headaches, it may be time for a professional eye check-up.

Vision problems in children can affect concentration, confidence, reading ability, and academic performance if not identified early. Conditions like lazy eye, squint, refractive errors, or focusing issues can often be managed successfully with timely diagnosis and treatment.

One of the most dangerous things about glaucoma is that many people don’t realize they have it until vision damage has already started. Glaucoma is often called the “silent thief of sight” because it slowly damages the optic nerve without causing pain in the early stages.

Many patients continue daily life normally while gradually losing side vision over time. By the time symptoms become noticeable, permanent damage may already have occurred. This is why regular eye pressure and optic nerve check-ups are extremely important, especially after the age of 40.

People with diabetes, high blood pressure, family history of glaucoma, or long-term steroid use may have a higher risk of developing glaucoma.

⚡ Retina Laser Treatment Explained — How It Helps Protect Vision

Retina laser treatment is a safe and advanced procedure used to treat various retinal conditions such as diabetic retinopathy, retinal tears, retinal leakage, and abnormal blood vessel growth inside the eye. The goal of laser treatment is to stabilize the retina and prevent further vision damage.

During the procedure, focused laser energy is applied to specific areas of the retina to seal leaking blood vessels or reduce abnormal vessel formation. The treatment is usually performed as an outpatient procedure and often does not require hospitalization.
